content.value:
A Zone is a geometric region on the field — a rectangle, polygon, or circle.

Zones represent real field elements like scoring areas, parking zones, or launch regions. Instead of guessing where the robot is, you check zone membership: "is the robot inside the launch zone?"

Marrow provides PolygonZone, CircleZone, and CompositeZone.

All zone types implement Zone.

contains(Point p) — is a single point inside the zone?

isInside(Zone other) — does this zone overlap with another? Use when the robot is also a zone.

isFullyInside(Zone other) — is this zone completely inside another? Stricter than isInside().

distanceTo(Point p) — shortest distance to the boundary. Returns 0 if inside.

distanceTo(Zone other) — shortest distance between two zone boundaries.

distanceToBoundary(Point p) — distance to the edge, even when inside.

moveBy(dx, dy) / setPosition(x, y) — translate the zone.
PolygonZone is created from points. Here, a triangle represents the close launch zone from the 2025–2026 DECODE field.

steps.title: Representing the robot as a zone

content.value: The robot itself is a PolygonZone — an 18x18 inch square. Its position is synced to the follower's pose every tick in run(), so it moves with the robot.

steps.title: Trigger: enter fires a command, exit cancels

content.value:
Trigger wraps a BooleanSupplier. whileActiveContinuous() schedules the command when the condition becomes true and cancels when it becomes false.

No wasInside boolean. No manual state tracking. Trigger handles edge detection.

Start the OpMode. Drive the robot with the gamepad.

The close launch zone is a triangle between (0, 141.5), (70.75, 70.75), and (141.5, 141.5).

Drive into it — "Inside close launch zone" appears in telemetry. Drive out — it disappears. The Trigger handles the enter/exit transition automatically.

What's the difference between isInside() and isFullyInside()?
options: isInside needs partial overlap; isFullyInside needs the entire zone inside
